I've been looking a long time at writing as a hobby, as a profession, and even from a stand-point of entertainment, yet I've not been blind to a growing trend in internet-writing culture. The rise of sites like hitRECord and Patreon has returned patronage from the ashes as a format for the writer to eke out a living. Even self-publishing has helped wrest power from the era of publishing as "a company" and delivered it back into the hands of those who actually create and consume writing.

However, as is, the system is only half complete. We write, even at a professional level, in a way that gives us "light" contact with our intended audiences (I am not speaking of customer interaction, but from a stand-point of ideas and story.) Stories are written about a myriad of topics, but it is not always the case that readers will read them. In bygone eras, storytellers took on a somewhat different role toward their demographic. A storyteller, sometimes a wanderer or on retainer, delivered crafted tales and those made up on the spot to the joy of their audience. It was far from a perfect system, but it was equally as far from boring.

That other half does exist today, and it's a huge venue. Forums such as /r/WritingPrompts and /v/WritingPrompts are a swarming mass of people crying out for storytellers, planting seeds for their own personal bedtime tales. The margin of prompts-to-writers may not be a staggering disproportion, but it definitely exists. And it's a treasure trove of Ali Baba-esque size just waiting for the right words.

Yet no one speaks, or at least, no one is openly dangling the keys in front of everyone's faces. And honestly, I'm grateful. I'm not going say that I wouldn't like to be one of those Woolf writers, sitting in a furnished room with a steady stream of funds freeing me from the consequences of life. That would be amazing. I will however say that I, like many others, benefit from the status quo. The free-trade of ideas is beautiful for a writer, as is the warm, fuzzy feeling of telling someone a story. I don't know if I'd be allowed to do that if WritingPrompts was a monetized, commission-based system. I've got a lot of self-doubt when it comes to writing, and current standards suit me fine.

But it's out there, this ephemeral Wild-West of commissioned writing. A strong figure could easily start a following of readers collected from the 3 million+ subscribers floating across sites, and if Twitch/Youtube is any indication of the shape that would take-- it stupefies me. Writers earning thousands (I understand that this number is not entirely realistic) not from novels, collections, or poetry, but from prompts crafted to give someone what they want. So what do you all think? Am I mad, or just stating something everyone has thought of but can't seem to jump-start?

TL;DR: Crazy person checking in with crazy ideas about WritingPrompts as a venue for commissioned writing, and secretly dreading the day when a "Pewdiepie" stakes their claims to it. Until then, we should all carry on like nothing is there. Shhhhhh!

If we want to support cross-posting in case the submission really is relevant to several subverses, the idea is that the submission could be tagged with several subverses, and the posts on each subverses would lead to the same discussion page. Comments would be shared between subverses, and the different communities would be allowed to interact with each other about a particular subject.

If something like this is implemented, I'm not sure if it should be the default / only way to cross post among subverses or if good old cross posting should still be possible because maybe you don't always want to share the discussion between the communities.

What do you think?
Let's really share posts across subverses instead of cross-posting them

I like this idea, maybe it would also make things easier if it were somehow automated instead of "I post in the subverse, then I copy the post (remember to add the cross-post info) to another subverse, rinse and repeat." handling that we have now.
You're right, this process is not convenient at all, it could be made easier, and hopefully sharing the discussion across communities would bring more relevant content.

The point of subverses is to separate communities.

Recently, there was a post about obesity potentially overtaking smoking as the leading cause of cancer.

This was posted in both /v/news, a community dedicated to discussing and sharing news, and to that ridiculous community dedicated to insulting people above a certain BMI.

In one sub, it was an opportunity to discuss the merits and implications of the article. In the other, it was any opportunity to spread hatred.

I, like many others, have zero interest in seeing the opinions from people in that second community.

Nothing's stopping anyone from posting link to a submission in other subverses. This isn't the common practice, however, because people recognize that communities should remain separate. If someone from that second community would like to submit their opinions to /v/news, they are welcome, but should not be encouraged to do so.

I understand your point. I believe the original poster decides what kind of conversation he wants to open, if he wants to involve hateful communities, well that's the kind of discussion he's offering. Hopefully not everyone is interested in the same thing and relevant discussion can also happen between consenting, serious communities.

Your comment convinced me that this idea should never be the mandatory, only way to cross-post, but rather an opportunity if you are really willing to share the discussion.
